title: Encode and Decode Strings
summary: Implement encode(strs), which turns a list of strings into one string, and decode(encoded), which rebuilds the original list from that string alone.

contract.output: string array from decode. Encode returns a string.

contractDetails.result: string array from decode. Encode returns a string.
contractDetails.constraints: 0–99 items, each 0–199 characters. The public NeetCode reference describes a 256-character alphabet as ASCII. Ycoders fixtures interpret it as character codes U+0000–U+00FF, with one code point per byte value. The validator compares the decoded list in its original order. C uses length-bearing byte strings.
contractDetails.output-checking: Use the encoder output as the only argument to a fresh decoder and compare its result with the original list. The intermediate encoding must be a string.

statement: Implement encode(strs), which turns a list of strings into one string, and decode(encoded), which rebuilds the original list from that string alone. Empty lists, empty items, repeated items and all allowed characters must survive the round trip. The decoder receives an encoding produced by your encoder. The encoding format is your choice.

examples.explanation: Punctuation and the empty item survive with their positions intact.
The decoder must reconstruct a list containing zero items.
Two empty payloads still occupy two positions.

constraints: 0–99 items, each 0–199 characters. The public NeetCode reference describes a 256-character alphabet as ASCII. Ycoders fixtures interpret it as character codes U+0000–U+00FF, with one code point per byte value. The validator compares the decoded list in its original order. C uses length-bearing byte strings.
hints: Conceptual: The decoder must distinguish an empty list from a list containing one empty string.
Directional: Store item lengths so a separator inside a payload cannot end the item early.
Implementation: Write a decimal length followed by a marker and exactly that many characters. Read the length first, then jump past the payload.
complexityAnalysis: O(L + n) time per operation for the length-prefixed representation, with L input characters across n items. A buffered encoder can use O(L + n) auxiliary space and the decoder O(1) excluding output.
